Audit the InkOS codebase at /Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/InkOS against the operations spec described below. Goal: produce a concrete "EXISTS vs MISSING vs PARTIAL" map per module so I can build a 50-100 sprint plan.

The PDF spec (InkOS_In_Practice.pdf) defines the target product as 16 modules in 5 clusters:

**THE HUB**
1. Dashboard — KPI tiles, Live Now widget, today's bookings timeline, BBP cert + ink expiry alerts
2. Inbox — UNIFIED multi-channel: Instagram DM, WhatsApp, Email, SMS, phone-note threads. Channel-tagged messages. AI Assist drafts. Send Message modal warns on channel mismatch. "Create Client from Thread."
3. Calendar — per-artist columns color-coded, deposit-gated booking (no card no slot), drag-to-reschedule, lunch/break auto-blocks, public booking widget at portfolio.inkos.studio
4. Messages — per-client view of all communications across all channels (client-centric dual to channel-centric Inbox)

**THE DATA**
5. Projects — multi-session work as one container. DEPOSIT POOL (In/Applied/Available/Refundable, 4 numbers tracked). Photo Progression timeline (refs+stencil+fresh+healed per session). Status: Planning→Active→Completed→Archived
6. Clients — list + 8-TAB DETAIL: Overview · Appointments · Photos · Notes (color-coded pinned) · Files · Comms · Consent · Financial. PERSISTENT ALLERGIES BANNER across all tabs (red, can only be cleared by authorized edit, logged)
7. Team — 3 artist types (Resident, Guest, Shop Staff), 3 comp models (Commission %, Booth Rental, Payroll/W-2). Tracks BBP cert expiry, state license #, Stripe Connect status, photo release defaults, permissions, 1099 vs W-2 flag

**PUBLIC FACE**
8. Flash & Portfolio — studio gallery + per-artist public pages at portfolio.inkos.studio/[studio]/[artist], SEO-indexed, bookable flash with deposit-gated claim
9. Flash Events — limited-time pop-up flash days (Friday 13th, Halloween, holidays), pop-up calendar block + landing page
10. Forms — 8 templates: New Client Intake, Standard Tattoo Consent, Photo Release (granular toggles: portfolio yes/IG yes/face obscured), REACH Ink Disclosure, GDPR Consent, Guardian Consent for Minors, Aftercare Acknowledgment, Pre-Session Health Check. Sent via SMS/email magic link, signed digitally with audit hash

**THE MONEY**
11. Payments — Stripe Connect destination charges, deposit pool draw + new charge combined at session settlement, commission splits (70/30 etc), tip routing (100% artist by default), tax sub-ledger per location, dispute defense pack auto-bundling, refund flow with proportional commission reversal, 1099-NEC export. Pricing models: hourly/per-piece/half-day/full-day/project-flat/walk-in-min. 8 charge types: deposit, top-up, balance settlement, tip, no-show, refund, chargeback, retail
12. Inventory (Studio+) — ink batches by manufacturer/lot/color/REACH-MoCRA status, gloves/needles/Saniderm tracking, low-stock alerts, REACH compliance log per ink batch
13. Analytics (Studio+) — artist utilisation, piece profitability by style/size/artist, cohort retention 30/90/365, no-show rate, deposit-to-revenue ratio, channel attribution, top clients by LTV

**INTELLIGENCE**
14. Marketing (Studio+) — automated flows: win-back, loyalty (points + tier credits), birthday cards, review capture (Google+IG). Visual editor for emails/SMS in studio brand template. Segment builder pulling from Analytics
15. AI Assist (Pro+) — 3 jobs: (1) drafts inbound replies in studio/artist voice learned from prior conversations (2) summarises consult to 3-bullet brief into Notes tab (3) auto-generates personalised aftercare from session data. NEVER sends autonomously
16. Settings — studio identity, hours, locations, tax rates per location, commission templates, payout schedules, cancellation policies (default 3 tiers: >48h full credit / 24-48h 50% / <24h full forfeit), deposit rules, kiosk/iPad config, public booking widget customisation, integrations (Stripe Connect, Meta, WhatsApp, Twilio, Mailchimp), GDPR/CCPA retention, user permissions, audit log

**KEY CROSS-CUTTING WORKFLOWS**
- 30-minute pre-session briefing push (allergies banner top, pinned notes, last 3 sessions, project state, deposit pool, forms outstanding, card on file)
- iPad kiosk check-in: phone number lookup, 3 forms one signature, hash + timestamp
- Day-14 healed photo SMS prompt
- Client portal via SMS magic link (no app, no login) — shows project, deposit pool, photo timeline, next appointment, aftercare, consent forms read-only
- Project completion automation: 30-day final-healed prompt, photo release confirmation, Google review prompt at day 7, loyalty points credit, 3-month referral incentive, 6-month win-back, birthday card
- Multi-tenancy: studio_id is the workspace boundary; RLS everywhere

**WHAT TO CHECK IN THE CODEBASE**

Walk through these directories and report what's built vs missing:

1. `app/(app)/` — which routes exist? Look for /dashboard, /inbox, /calendar, /messages, /clients, /projects, /team, /flash, /forms, /payments, /inventory, /analytics, /marketing, /ai-assist, /settings/*. The CLAUDE.md mentions /reports/* exists and /bookings/* exists — verify and identify what's missing vs PDF.
2. `app/(app)/clients/` — does the 8-tab detail page exist? Which tabs? Allergies banner persistence?
3. `app/api/` — which endpoints exist? Check inbox, calendar, projects, payments, inventory, marketing folders. The git status shows api/inventory, api/marketing, api/reports modified.
4. `components/` — which feature folders exist? inventory, marketing, reports show in git status. Look for inbox, calendar, projects, team, flash, forms, payments components.
5. `lib/billing/feature-gate.ts` — read it, list 23 KNOWN_FEATURE_KEYS, map them to PDF features.
6. `supabase/migrations/` — list all migrations, identify schema for: studios, users (artists/owners/clients), bookings, sessions, projects, clients, deposits/deposit_pool, payments, photos, notes, forms, consent, inventory, ink_batches, marketing_campaigns.
7. `lib/dodo/` — confirm Dodo Payments client exists (CLAUDE.md says Dodo). Note: PDF assumes Stripe Connect for marketplace splits — flag this conflict.
8. `proxy.ts`, `middleware.ts` — what's gating routes?
9. Search for any "deposit_pool" or "DepositPool" references — does the pool concept exist as a first-class entity?
10. Search for "allergies" and "allergy_banner" — is the persistent banner already wired?
11. Search for AI Assist / Anthropic — current implementation surface?
12. Search for Instagram / WhatsApp / Twilio integration — do any exist? (Inbox unification is a huge gap risk.)
13. Search for "kiosk" — does kiosk mode exist?
14. Search for "portfolio" public route — does portfolio.inkos.studio per-artist page exist?
15. Search for "photo_timeline" / "session_photos" — schema for refs+stencil+fresh+healed?
16. Search for "1099" / "tax_export" / "stripe_connect" — earnings/payout tooling?
17. Read `~/.claude/memory/projects/inkos-lessons.md` if it exists — extract recurring antipatterns and known gaps.
18. Check `scripts/seed/demo/README.md` — what feature areas have demo data already?

REPORT FORMAT (target ~600 words):

For each of the 16 modules, give a 2-3 line verdict:
- ✅ EXISTS — list 2-3 sub-features that work today
- 🟡 PARTIAL — list what exists, list what's missing
- ❌ MISSING — confirm not built

Then a separate "CRITICAL GAPS" section listing:
- Architecture pieces that don't exist yet (deposit pool entity? unified inbox? Stripe Connect? kiosk mode? AI assist? client portal magic link? portfolio public page?)
- Data model gaps (which tables clearly missing from migrations)
- Integration gaps (Instagram/WhatsApp/Twilio/Stripe Connect)
- Migration risks (existing /reports vs new /analytics?  existing /marketing vs new structure?)

Then a "NOTABLE CONFLICTS" section:
- Stripe Connect (PDF) vs Dodo Payments (CLAUDE.md) — for in-studio client charges + commission splits
- Anything else that contradicts CLAUDE.md

Use exact file paths so I can navigate quickly. Skip prose, just findings.

1	# InkOS — Project Context for Claude Code
2	
3	> This file is **project-specific only**. Global agent routing, Stack A conventions,
4	> and build standards live in `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` and are not duplicated here.
5	> If it is unique to InkOS — mission, brand, product model, gotchas — it lives here.
6	> If it applies to every Boldteq Stack A project, it lives in the global file.
7	
8	**Stack:** A (Next.js 16.2.3 + Supabase + Railway + Dodo Payments)
9	**Status:** Sprint 12 complete — launch-ready
10	**Scaffolded by:** Riko on 2026-04-15
11	**Build plan:** `~/.claude/plans/immutable-conjuring-pelican.md` (12 sprints — ALL COMPLETE)
12	**Lessons:** `~/.claude/memory/projects/inkos-lessons.md` (load on every touch)
13	**Brand Board authority:** `InkOS_Brand_Board.pdf` v1.0 · Locked April 2026
14	
15	---
16	
17	## 1. What InkOS Is
18	
19	**InkOS is the operating system for modern tattoo studios.** Multi-tenant SaaS replacing
20	the fragmented tools (DaySmart / Tattoo Studio Pro / Porter / Fresha / Booksy) that studio
21	owners currently glue together with spreadsheets and Venmo.
22	
23	**Who it's for**
24	- **Studio owners** — running a shop with 1–20 artists, tired of Fresha's 2025 pricing churn,
25	  tired of Porter charging $250 for payroll they rarely use.
26	- **Artists** (resident + guest) — booking clients, managing portfolios, tracking commissions.
27	- **Receptionists** — front-desk booking, consent forms, payments, inventory.
28	
29	**Multi-user from day 1.** No single-seat fallback. Every studio ships with owner +
30	artist + receptionist roles at signup.
31	
32	**Where it runs**
33	- Authenticated web app (no v1 marketing pages — waitlist only at `/`).
34	- Client-facing public booking at `/book/[studioSlug]` (anonymous).
35	- Digital consent forms at `/consent/[token]` (anonymous).
36	- Team invites at `/invite/[token]` (anonymous).
37	
38	**Tagline** (in `app/layout.tsx` metadata):
39	> "The operating system for modern tattoo studios."
40	
41	---
42	
43	## 2. Strategic Moats — Why We Win
44	
45	Five durable advantages from the build plan. Every product/design decision must
46	reinforce at least one of these. If a proposed feature dilutes them, reject it.
47	
48	1. **AI Design Assistant** — Claude-powered moodboards + reference search, included at
49	   Pro ($99). No competitor ships this natively.
50	2. **Full payroll + 1099-K at $99** — Porter charges $250. We commoditize it.
51	3. **EU REACH ink passports + GDPR-native** — First EU-compliant studio OS. Porter and
52	   Fresha are US-first; we ship compliance day 1.
53	4. **Transparent flat pricing** — Post-Fresha 2025 pricing-churn event, studios want
54	   predictable costs. Four tiers, no per-seat surprise fees.
55	5. **Guest artist module at $99** — Porter charges $250 separately. We include it.
56	
57	---
58	
59	## 3. Pricing & Feature Gates (LOCKED)
60	
61	**Four tiers, locked:**
62	
63	| Tier | Price/mo | Positioning |
64	|------|----------|-------------|
65	| Solo | $29 | Single artist, essentials only |
66	| Studio | $59 | Multi-artist operations |
67	| Pro | $99 | AI + payroll + compliance — the anchor tier |
68	| Enterprise | $199 | Multi-location + white-label + API |
69	
70	**Feature-gate source of truth:** [lib/billing/feature-gate.ts](lib/billing/feature-gate.ts) — 23 keys in `KNOWN_FEATURE_KEYS`.
71	
72	**Always-on (all tiers, not gated):**
73	`booking` · `calendar` · `public_booking_page` · `digital_consent` · `client_crm` · `dodo_payments` · `custom_domain`
74	
75	**Studio+ (min plan `studio`):**
76	`inventory` · `commissions` · `sms_reminders` · `marketing_basic` · `marketing_advanced` · `calendar_sync` · `referral_program`
77	
78	**Pro+ (min plan `pro`):**
79	`payroll` · `ai_design` · `ai_design_assistant` · `guest_artists` · `eu_reach` · `multi_location` · `analytics`
80	
81	**Enterprise (min plan `enterprise`):**
82	`white_label` · `api_access`
83	
84	**Gating rule (non-negotiable):**
85	- **Server:** API routes call `requireFeatureRpc(supabase, studioId, key)` — throws `FeatureGateError` → 403.
86	- **UI:** Wrap gated components in `<FeatureGate feature="…">` fallback. Never hardcode `plan === 'pro'` checks anywhere.
87	- Dual-layer is mandatory: UI hide + server reject. One layer is a bypass.
88	
89	---
90	
91	## 4. Brand System v1.0 — LOCKED April 2026
92	
93	Source of truth: **InkOS Brand Board v1.0** (PDF) + [app/globals.css](app/globals.css) `@theme inline`.
94	If any design or marketing output breaks this section, Vega / Pixel / Quill / Sage must reject it.
95	
96	### 4.1 Palette — the 60/20/15/5 rule
97	
98	| Color | Hex | Share | Token | Where it appears |
99	|-------|-----|-------|-------|------------------|
100	| **Bone**  | `#F7F7F5` | 60% | `--color-bone` | Page background, sidebar background, card surfaces, empty states. The canvas. |
101	| **Onyx**  | `#0F0F0F` | 20% | `--color-onyx` | Primary text, headlines, KPI numbers, primary CTAs (`+ New booking`), logo, workspace mark. |
102	| **Stone** | `#787774` | 15% | `--color-stone` | Secondary text, labels, metadata, section headers ("STUDIO", "OPERATIONS"), borders. |
103	| **Rust**  | `#B23A2B` | 5%  | `--color-rust` | Active nav state, LIVE pulse, "NOW" sweep bar, accent border on hero KPI, destructive CTA. **Once or twice per viewport max.** |
104	
105	**Forbidden:**
106	- `#FFFFFF` — use Bone `#F7F7F5` instead.
107	- `#000000` — use Onyx `#0F0F0F` instead.
108	- **Any color outside the four above.** No additions. No substitutes. No brand purple, teal,
109	  "accent blue", success green (use Onyx text on Bone bg with a green dot if you must).
110	- Gradients — solid surfaces only.
111	- Raw hex literals in components — always use semantic tokens from `globals.css`.
112	
113	**Semantic derivations** (already wired in [app/globals.css](app/globals.css)):
114	`--color-primary` = Onyx · `--color-destructive` = Rust · `--color-accent` = Rust @ 8%
115	opacity · `--color-muted-foreground` = Stone · `--color-border` = Stone-tinted.
116	
117	### 4.2 Typography
118	
119	| Family | Weights | Use |
120	|--------|---------|-----|
121	| **Inter** | 400 / 500 / 600 / 700 / 800 | Everything except display moments. Primary workhorse. |
122	| **Instrument Serif** | 400 roman + italic | Page titles, italic accent words, empty-state names. **Display only.** |
123	| **JetBrains Mono** | 400 / 500 | Code, logs, API responses. Never UI copy. |
124	
125	**Type scale** (all tokens live in [app/globals.css](app/globals.css)):
126	
127	| Token | Font | Size | Weight | Use |
128	|-------|------|------|--------|-----|
129	| `display` | Instrument Serif | 52px | 400 | Dashboard hero: *"The studio, at a glance."* |
130	| `page-title` | Instrument Serif | 36px | 400 | Empty-state names: *"Artists & Team"*, *"Calendar"* |
131	| `kpi` | Inter | 52px | 800 | Dashboard numbers: `$8,320`, `87`, `94` |
132	| `h2` | Inter | 24px | 700 | Section titles inside pages |
133	| `h3` | Inter | 16px | 700 | Card titles, list headers |
134	| `body` | Inter | 14px | 400 | Descriptions, paragraphs |
135	| `label` | Inter | 11px | 700 | Uppercase, `tracking-0.08em` — "TODAY'S REVENUE", "STUDIO", "GROWTH" |
136	| `caption` | Inter | 12px | 400 | Metadata, timestamps — *"vs. last Tue"* |
137	
138	**Rules:**
139	- **Tabular figures on every number** (KPIs, prices, counts) — `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums`.
140	- **Never serif on body text, labels, or data.** Serif is for moments, not paragraphs.
141	- **Italicize emphasis words, never full sentences.** The italic carries tone, not volume.
142	- Example of correct serif use: *"Four colors. Locked."* · *"The signature."* · *"The rules."*
143	
144	### 4.3 Logo & Mark
145	
146	**The mark:** lowercase italic `i` in a filled tile. One shape works at every size.
147	
148	**Lockups:**
149	- **Horizontal** — tile + "InkOS" wordmark + "Studio OS" subtitle (sidebar brandmark, email signature if 24px+).
150	- **Wordmark only** — *i*nkOS (marketing hero where tile would compete).
151	- **Stacked mono** — Onyx tile with Rust `i` + white "InkOS" (dark hero sections, onboarding).
152	
153	**Tile variants:**
154	- `i` on Bone (default, light backgrounds).
155	- `i` on Onyx (dark hero, sidebar expanded, loading states).
156	- `i` on Rust (rare — only for brand-identity moments like favicons on dark mode UAs).
157	
158	**Sizing:**
159	
160	| Context | Size | Notes |
161	|---------|------|-------|
162	| Favicon / app icon | 16–64px | Mark only, no wordmark, no subtitle |
163	| Sidebar brandmark | 32px tile | With wordmark beside + "Studio OS" subtitle below |
164	| Marketing hero | 48px+ tile | Full horizontal lockup |
165	| Email signature | 24px tile | Inline with wordmark only, no subtitle |
166	
167	**Clear space:** padding on all sides ≥ 0.5× tile height. Don't crowd the mark.
168	
169	### 4.4 The 4 Brand Rules (reject anything that breaks these)
170	
171	1. **Editorial polish, not corporate template.**
172	   InkOS looks like a magazine editor built a CRM. Serif italic accents · Bone background
173	   instead of sterile white · restrained color use. **Never** generic SaaS purple. **Never**
174	   Fresha-energetic. **Never** rainbow-gradient landing heroes.
175	
176	2. **Rust is earned, never decorative.**
177	   Every use of `#B23A2B` must answer: *"is this the active state, the live indicator, or
178	   the critical anchor?"* If no — it's not Rust. Use Onyx or Stone instead.
179	
180	3. **Onyx buttons carry the workflow.**
181	   Primary CTAs (`+ New booking`, `Approve`, `Save`) are Onyx, not Rust. Rust CTAs are
182	   reserved for rare destructive-accent moments (`Delete permanently`, `Revoke access`).
183	   Black buttons on Bone = premium B2B. Red everywhere = consumer app.
184	
185	4. **Serif shows up in moments, not paragraphs.**
186	   Instrument Serif is for page titles, italic accent words, empty-state names.
187	   **Never** body text, **never** labels, **never** numbers. Inter carries the workload;
188	   the serif carries the personality.
189	
190	### 4.5 Motion
191	
192	**The "NOW" sweep bar is the only motion on the dashboard.** 2px vertical line + pulsing
193	10px dot, both Rust, sweeping across the current time in `/dashboard` timeline.
194	Nothing else animates on the main dashboard. No spinners on hover. No carousel
195	autoscroll. No confetti. No gradient shifts. Stillness is the brand.
196	
197	Elsewhere: keep motion functional — route transitions, toast slide-in, drawer open.
198	Never decorative. 150ms default, `ease-out`.
199	
200	### 4.6 Shadow tokens (never use default Tailwind shadows)
201	
202	| Token | Use |
203	|-------|-----|
204	| `shadow-soft` | Hairline card borders, inputs |
205	| `shadow-card` | Standard card elevation on Bone |
206	| `shadow-card-hover` | Card hover lift |
207	| `shadow-soft-md` | Drawers, modals |
208	| `shadow-lift` | Command palette, toasts, tooltips |
209	| `shadow-overlay` | Modal backdrops |
210	
211	**Forbidden:** `shadow-sm`, `shadow-md`, `shadow-lg`, `shadow-xl`, `shadow-2xl` — Tailwind defaults are too blue and too heavy for Bone.
212	
213	### 4.7 Do / Don't
214	
215	**DO**
216	- Use Bone as the default page background — everywhere.
217	- Pair Onyx headlines with Stone subtitles for quiet hierarchy.
218	- Reserve Rust for one or two elements per viewport.
219	- Use Instrument Serif only on page titles + italic emphasis.
220	- Keep the "NOW" sweep bar as the only motion on the dashboard.
221	- Use tabular figures on every number (KPIs, prices, counts).
222	
223	**DON'T**
224	- Add any color outside Bone / Rust / Stone / Onyx.
225	- Use Rust as a button background (except rare destructive).
226	- Italicize full sentences — emphasis words only.
227	- Use Instrument Serif on body text, labels, or data.
228	- Use pure white (`#FFFFFF`) — always Bone.
229	- Use pure black (`#000000`) — always Onyx.
230	
231	---
232	
233	## 5. UI Philosophy (how every screen is built)
234	
235	- **Solid surfaces only** — no gradients, no glassmorphism, no frosted blur.
236	- **Hairline Stone borders** — `--color-border` at Stone-tinted opacity. No heavy strokes.
237	- **Light mode default.** Dark mode is theme-toggle secondary — honor tokens but don't design dark-first.
238	- **KPI cards** — Onyx number (Inter 800, tabular), Stone label (uppercase, tracked `0.08em`),
239	  optional Rust 2px left border on the single hero KPI per viewport.
240	- **One Rust accent per viewport, maximum two.** If you need a third, you're designing wrong.
241	- **All tokens live in [app/globals.css](app/globals.css) `@theme inline`** — Tailwind 4, no `tailwind.config.ts`, ever.
242	- **Spacing** — page padding `1.5rem` desktop / `1rem` mobile; card padding `1.5rem`; section gap `1.5rem`.
243	- **Sidebar** — `16rem` desktop (S24, was `15rem`), `19rem` mobile drawer, `3.5rem` icon-mode. Bone background, Rust active state at 8% opacity. Keep CSS vars (`--sidebar-width*` in [app/globals.css](app/globals.css)) in lockstep with JS constants in [components/ui/sidebar.tsx](components/ui/sidebar.tsx) — SidebarProvider writes them as inline styles, so drift silently breaks collapse transitions.
244	
245	---
246	
247	## 6. Voice & Copy — Quill Reference
248	
249	**Tone:** editorial, quiet, confident. Never hype. Never exclamation marks. Never "Amazing!".
250	
251	**Cadence:** short sentences. Periods, not commas, carry rhythm. Italics earn their place.
252	
253	**Examples of correct display copy (from the brand board):**
254	- *"The studio, at a glance."*
255	- *"Today's schedule — Tuesday, April 21 · noon–midnight"*
256	- *"Six chairs running. One guest from Mumbai. Three bookings flagged for a gentle nudge."*
257	- *"The brand, in full."*
258	- *"Four colors. Locked."*
259	
260	**Numbers stand alone.** `$8,320` · `87%` · `94` — Inter 800, tabular, no decorative prefix.
261	
262	**Microcopy rules:**
263	- Primary CTA verbs: "Book", "Save", "Send", "Approve". Not "Click here", not "Submit".
264	- Empty states: serif name + one-sentence editorial explanation. No illustrations with shrug emojis.
265	- Error messages: factual, no "Oops!". Example: *"Deposit couldn't be processed. The card was declined by the issuer."*
266	- Email subject lines: no emojis, no ALL CAPS, no "🔥 Last chance!".
267	
268	Quill owns marketing landing / email / social / in-app microcopy.
269	Pixel owns the 14 public-page copy structures under Quill's voice.
270	
271	---
272	
273	## 7. Architecture Decisions (project-specific)
274	
275	1. **Next.js 16 uses `proxy.ts` not `middleware.ts`** — at project root, not in `app/`.
276	2. **`cookies()` is async in Next 16** — always `await cookies()`.
277	3. **Worker packages NEVER import `next/*`** — separate `package.json` in `workers/jobs/` and `workers/cron/`.
278	4. **BullMQ ioredis requires `maxRetriesPerRequest: null`** — silent failure without it.
279	5. **Supabase service-role client bypasses RLS** — only in webhook handlers + admin ops.
280	6. **Webhook handler uses `timingSafeEqual`** — constant-time HMAC comparison, never `===`.
281	7. **`subscriptions` table is write-only by webhook** — no app code writes to it directly.
282	8. **Tailwind 4 — no `tailwind.config.ts`** — all tokens in [app/globals.css](app/globals.css) `@theme inline` only.
283	
284	---
285	
286	## 8. Forbidden (Sage hard-fails on review)
287	
288	- `@supabase/auth-helpers-nextjs` — use `@supabase/ssr`
289	- Vercel — use Railway
290	- Stripe — use Dodo Payments
291	- NextAuth — use Supabase Auth
292	- Prisma / any ORM — use Supabase client + generated types
293	- Pages Router — App Router only
294	- npm / yarn — pnpm only
295	- CSS modules — Tailwind only
296	- `any` TypeScript — zero exceptions
297	- `console.log` — use [lib/logger.ts](lib/logger.ts) (pino)
298	- **Raw hex literals in components** — use tokens from `globals.css`. Only `globals.css` itself defines hexes, and only for Bone / Onyx / Stone / Rust.
299	- `tailwind.config.ts` — Tailwind 4 lives in `@theme inline` only.
300	- Default Tailwind shadows (`shadow-sm`, `shadow-md`, etc.) — use `shadow-soft` / `shadow-card` / `shadow-soft-md`.
301	- Hardcoded plan-tier checks (`plan === 'pro'`) — use `hasFeature(plan, key)` or `<FeatureGate>`.
302	- Hand-edits to [lib/supabase/types.ts](lib/supabase/types.ts) — regenerate with `pnpm db:types`.
303	
304	---
305	
306	## 9. Recurring Antipatterns (from `inkos-lessons.md`)
307	
308	Load `~/.claude/memory/projects/inkos-lessons.md` on every touch. The traps we keep hitting:
309	
310	- **Never hand-edit [lib/supabase/types.ts](lib/supabase/types.ts)** — always `pnpm db:types` after any Dato migration.
311	- **RPC-only writes for audit-critical tables** — `bookings`, `payments`, `payroll`, `consent`. Direct `.insert()` bypasses audit trigger.
312	- **Dual-layer feature gate mandatory** — server `requireFeatureRpc()` + UI `<FeatureGate>`. One layer is a bypass.
313	- **Public routes use anonymous Supabase client** — `/book/[slug]`, `/consent/[token]`, `/invite/[token]`. Never the session-cookie server client.
314	- **Define RPC contracts as shared TS interfaces BEFORE Dato writes the migration.** Contract drift = runtime 500s.
315	- **Dodo Payments gotchas:**
316	  - Follow `standardwebhooks` spec exactly (webhook-id + webhook-timestamp + webhook-signature headers).
317	  - Checkout param is `return_url`, **not** `success_url`.
318	  - Customer portal call returns `{ link }`, not `{ url }`.
319	  - Lazy-init the Dodo client — it throws if constructed before env vars load.
320	  - `billing.country` is required on customer create — ISO 3166 two-letter code.
321	- **`asChild` violations** — shadcn `<Button asChild>` must wrap exactly one child. Wrapping `<Link><Icon/> text</Link>` breaks Slot.
322	- **Rate-limit every public route** — use `apiRatelimit` from [lib/rate-limit.ts](lib/rate-limit.ts). Missing this is the #1 Sage hard-fail on public endpoints.
323	
324	---

1	/**
2	 * Server-side feature gating.
3	 *
4	 * DEV MODE (current): all server-side gates are pass-through — every feature is
5	 * open to every plan. Badges in the sidebar/nav are still computed via static
6	 * `hasFeature()` for visual indication of "this would be gated in prod".
7	 *
8	 * To re-enable restrictions: revert `requireFeatureRpc`, `checkFeatureRpc`, and
9	 * `requireFeature` to their original RPC-backed implementations (see git history).
10	 *
11	 * NEVER call check_feature_access from Client Components — server-side only.
12	 */
13	
14	import type { SupabaseClient } from '@supabase/supabase-js'
15	import { logger } from '@/lib/logger'
16	
17	export type PlanTier = 'solo' | 'studio' | 'pro' | 'enterprise'
18	
19	export const PLAN_ORDER: Record<PlanTier, number> = {
20	  solo: 0,
21	  studio: 1,
22	  pro: 2,
23	  enterprise: 3,
24	}
25	
26	/**
27	 * Canonical set of feature keys — must match the plan features JSONB in the DB.
28	 * If this set drifts from DB values, requireFeatureRpc() will universally 403.
29	 * Run warnOnFeatureKeyDrift() at startup to surface any mismatch early.
30	 */
31	export const KNOWN_FEATURE_KEYS = new Set([
32	  'booking',
33	  'calendar',
34	  'public_booking_page',
35	  'digital_consent',
36	  'client_crm',
37	  'dodo_payments',
38	  'inventory',
39	  'commissions',
40	  'payroll',
41	  'ai_design',
42	  'ai_design_assistant',
43	  'guest_artists',
44	  'eu_reach',

46	  'custom_domain',
47	  'api_access',
48	  'sms_reminders',
49	  'analytics',
50	  'white_label',
51	  'marketing_basic',
52	  'marketing_advanced',
53	  'calendar_sync',
54	  'referral_program',
55	  'omnichannel_inbox',
56	  'messaging_ai_replies',
57	  'projects',
58	  'flash_events',
59	])

61	/**
62	 * Called at server startup (e.g. instrumentation.ts) to warn if plan JSONB
63	 * contains keys not in KNOWN_FEATURE_KEYS — catches future key drift early.
64	 * Never throws; degraded gracefully.
65	 */
66	export async function warnOnFeatureKeyDrift(supabase: SupabaseClient): Promise<void> {
67	  try {
68	    const { data, error } = await supabase
69	      .from('plans')
70	      .select('name, features')
71	      .eq('is_active', true)
72	    if (error || !data) return
73	
74	    for (const plan of data) {
75	      const keys = plan.features as string[] | null
76	      if (!Array.isArray(keys)) continue
77	      for (const key of keys) {
78	        if (!KNOWN_FEATURE_KEYS.has(key)) {
79	          logger.warn(
80	            { plan: plan.name, unknownKey: key },
81	            'feature-gate: plan contains unknown feature key — check_feature_access may 403 unexpectedly',
82	          )
83	        }
84	      }
85	    }
86	  } catch {
87	    // Startup check — never block server init
88	  }
89	}
90	
91	/** Minimum plan required for each feature key (static fallback) */
92	const FEATURE_MIN_PLAN: Record<string, PlanTier> = {
93	  inventory: 'studio',
94	  commissions: 'studio',
95	  payroll: 'pro',
96	  ai_design: 'pro',
97	  ai_design_assistant: 'pro',
98	  guest_artists: 'pro',

102	  api_access: 'enterprise',
103	  sms_reminders: 'studio',
104	  analytics: 'studio',

106	  marketing_advanced: 'studio',

108	  referral_program: 'studio',
109	  omnichannel_inbox: 'studio',
110	  messaging_ai_replies: 'pro',
111	  projects: 'pro',
112	  flash_events: 'studio',
113	}

115	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
116	// Static helpers (no DB round-trip)

118	
119	export function hasFeature(plan: PlanTier, feature: string): boolean {
120	  const minPlan = FEATURE_MIN_PLAN[feature]
121	  if (!minPlan) return true
122	  return PLAN_ORDER[plan] >= PLAN_ORDER[minPlan]
123	}
124	
125	export function requiredPlanFor(feature: string): PlanTier | null {
126	  return FEATURE_MIN_PLAN[feature] ?? null

132	  return null

142	    super(`Feature '${featureKey}' is not available on current plan`)
143	    this.name = 'FeatureGateError'

157	  _supabase: SupabaseClient,

160	): Promise<void> {

165	 * DEV MODE: always returns true.
166	 * Re-enable by reverting to the RPC-backed implementation.
